# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

I need to establish communication with Blind first, since I can only speak to Mute and Blind, and Blind just gestured to me. Let me acknowledge and describe what I see, since Blind can't see anything but can hear me.

Let me describe the bomb state clearly for Blind (who can hear me but not see gestures) and also inform Mute (who can hear me too, and can see gestures I make, but can't see the bomb itself - wait, Mute cannot see either, only hear and read manual). Let me re-check: Mute reads manual, cannot speak or touch. Mute presumably can see and hear? The table only lists "cannot" for each - Mute cannot speak or touch, implying Mute CAN see and hear. So Mute can see my gestures AND hear my speech.

I should report the bomb details via speech (Blind hears it, Mute hears it) and also gesture isn't needed since speech reaches both who need it (Blind and Mute).

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb status: display shows 0. Light is off. Plate has an engraving I can't identify yet, marked as a question mark symbol. Three wires: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Waiting for manual info from Mute.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✋]

Mute is sending me gestures - since Mute cannot speak, this is the only way Mute can communicate with me directly. I can see gestures. Let me think about what these might encode.

Three pairs of gestures: [☝ 👍], [✌ 👌], [🤟 ✋]. This could be encoding information about the three wires (1, 2, 3) with some instruction - perhaps ☝=one, ✌=two, 🤟=three (finger counting), and the second symbol in each pair indicates an action or status for that wire number.

☝ 👍 = wire 1: 👍 (good/cut/keep?)
✌ 👌 = wire 2: 👌 (ok?)
🤟 ✋ = wire 3: ✋ (stop/don't?)

This is ambiguous without more context. I don't have the manual, so I can't be sure what these gesture-codes mean. I should relay this to Blind as raw gesture information (blind gets blanks for gestures, so this won't help Blind directly), but I should also try to confirm interpretation - though I can't speak to Mute since Mute can't hear... wait, can Mute hear? Mute's cannot list is "speak, or touch" - implying Mute CAN hear and see. So I could gesture back to Mute to confirm, but let's check - can I gesture? Yes, deaf can gesture too presumably since not restricted. Let me try to confirm my interpretation by gesturing back.

Since it's turn order Mute, Blind, Deaf - my gestures now would land on... gestures reach whoever can see. Mute can see (only cannot speak/touch). Blind cannot see. So my gesture to Mute would work for confirmation, but only Mute would receive it next round.

Let me relay to Blind via speech what I observed (as blank-safe description), and try to confirm with Mute via gesture.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent me three gesture-pairs, likely about the three wires. I'll try to confirm meaning with Mute and relay actionable instructions to you soon.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✌", "👌", "🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute repeated just the second symbol from each pair: 👍, 👌, ✋. This confirms my guess was right - the first symbols (☝ ✌ 🤟) were indeed wire numbers 1, 2, 3, and now Mute is confirming the action/status for each: wire 1 = 👍, wire 2 = 👌, wire 3 = ✋.

This looks like a per-wire instruction:
- Wire 1 (yellow): 👍 = good/proceed/cut this one?
- Wire 2 (green): 👌 = ok/fine?
- Wire 3 (red): ✋ = stop/don't touch!

This strongly suggests: cut wire 1, wire 2 is okay (maybe secondary), wire 3 = danger, do NOT cut/touch.

But I need to be careful - this could also mean order of operations, or which one is safe vs dangerous. Given ✋ commonly means "stop", wire 3 (red) is very likely the dangerous one not to touch. 👍 suggests wire 1 is the correct one. 👌 could mean wire 2 is also fine/neutral.

I should relay this interpretation to Blind, since Blind is the one who acts. But I should be cautious about wording - I'll give the raw mapping and my best interpretation, letting Blind and Mute continue to refine.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is signaling per-wire status via gestures, matched to wire numbers by order. Wire 1 (yellow) got thumbs up. Wire 2 (green) got an OK sign. Wire 3 (red) got a stop hand. My read: wire 1 seems safe or correct to act on, wire 3 seems dangerous, do not touch it. Wait for more confirmation before acting.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]

Mute is confirming my thumbs-up (agreeing with my interpretation) and adding ✊ (fist) - this could mean "cut" or "grab/pull" as an action to perform. So the combined message might be: "Yes, correct - now cut/pull wire 1."

Let me pass this along to Blind with my best interpretation, while acknowledging uncertainty. Given the stakes, I should encourage Blind to wait for Mute's next signal too, since Blind can't hear Mute directly - I'm the relay for gestures, but Blind can hear my speech.

Wait, actually - can Blind hear? Blind's cannot list is "see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - implying Blind CAN hear speech. Good, so my speech reaches Blind directly.

I'll relay this new gesture and interpretation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just repeated thumbs up for wire 1 and added a fist gesture. My best guess: Mute is confirming wire 1 is correct, and the fist may mean cut or pull that wire. Wire 3 was marked stop, so avoid that one. Suggest we wait one more exchange to be sure, but this points to acting on wire 1, yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signaled wire 2 alone, right after I confirmed wire 1. This might mean I misunderstood, or wire 2 is next in sequence. Do not touch anything yet. I will try to get a clean confirmation on which single wire to cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute is saying 👎 (no, disagreeing with my wire-1 idea) then ✌ 👍 (wire 2 = thumbs up/correct). So the correct wire to cut is wire 2 (green), not wire 1. My earlier interpretation was wrong - the 👍👌✋ sequence must have meant something else, or Mute is now clarifying more precisely.

Let me relay this correction to Blind clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Correction: Mute rejected my wire 1 guess with thumbs down, then signaled wire 2 with thumbs up. So the correct wire is wire 2, the green one. Wire 3 red was marked stop earlier, avoid it. Recommend acting on wire 2, green, but let me get one more confirmation first.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✊]

Mute confirmed wire 2 with ✊ (the same action gesture used before with wire 1) - so ✊ likely means "cut". This is consistent: cut wire 2, the green wire.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: Mute signaled wire 2 with the cut gesture again. Cut wire 2, the green wire. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 3. This is our best reading, proceed with cutting wire 2 if you're ready.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✊", "👍"])
```
